items.topic: Violation prioritization strategy to reach score >= 70
items.context: With 151 violations and a target of >= 70 (not 100), we need to decide how to prioritize. The GCT scoring weights violation categories differently. Complex functions and long files are high-weight categories, while lint issues are lower-weight. Fixing the top 8 long files (all over 600 lines) and top 10 complex functions would address ~40% of violations but likely move the score significantly since those are the heaviest-weighted categories.

options.label: Fix all long_files first, then complex_functions by size descending
options.rationale: Long files are often the root cause of complex functions (splitting files naturally breaks up functions). Addresses both categories simultaneously. Start with orchestrator.go (1,364 lines) which has both the longest file AND most complex function.

options.label: Fix by impact score (lines * complexity) across all categories
options.rationale: Mathematically optimal but harder to execute — requires computing a composite score for each violation and jumping between files/categories.

options.label: Fix by component area (all API, then CLI, then UI)
options.rationale: Already the phased approach in the plan. Simpler to execute but may leave high-impact UI violations for last.

items.context: The lint_issues category includes 12 files with TypeScript 'as' type casts, mostly in ui/src/components/ui/ — these are shadcn components that were likely generated with 'as' casts by the component generator. Fixing them requires adding type guards or restructuring component props. However, shadcn components are semi-generated code that may be regenerated later, which could undo manual fixes.

options.label: Fix all 'as' casts with proper type guards
options.rationale: Thorough but fragile if shadcn components are regenerated. About 12 files to modify.

options.label: Add ESLint disable comments for shadcn/ui components, fix only non-generated files
options.rationale: Pragmatic — acknowledges these are generated components. Focus lint fixes on actual application code (GuidedFlow.tsx, selectors.ts, SwapSuggestions.test.tsx). Fewer changes, less risk of regressions.

options.label: Skip 'as' cast fixes entirely — focus lint effort on .golangci.yml and CRITICAL comments only
options.rationale: Minimizes UI changes. TypeScript 'as' casts are lower-weight in GCT scoring. May be enough if Go refactoring gets us to >= 70.

items.context: The plan has 5 phases but only checks GCT score at the end (Phase 5). If score >= 70 is reached after Phase 2 (API refactoring), Phases 3-4 may be unnecessary. Running GCT mid-phase helps decide whether to continue or stop early.

options.label: Run GCT after each phase and stop when score >= 70
options.rationale: Most efficient — stops as soon as the target is met. Avoids unnecessary refactoring. But GCT runs may add overhead.

options.label: Run GCT after Phase 2 (API) only, then decide
options.rationale: One checkpoint at the highest-impact point. If API refactoring alone gets to >= 70, skip CLI and UI phases.

options.label: Complete all phases regardless, check GCT at end
options.rationale: Ensures all areas are cleaned up. More work but more thorough.

items.context: Adding .golangci.yml is Phase 1. The configuration needs to balance catching real issues vs. being too noisy. Key linters to consider: funlen (function length), cyclop (cyclomatic complexity), gocognit (cognitive complexity), gocritic (code patterns), errcheck (unchecked errors).

options.label: Minimal config: funlen + cyclop + gocognit only
options.rationale: Directly targets the GCT violation categories (complex_functions, long_files). Won't flag new issues outside the refactoring scope. Simplest to get passing.

options.label: Standard config: funlen + cyclop + gocognit + gocritic + errcheck
options.rationale: More comprehensive linting. May surface additional issues that need fixing, increasing scope beyond the original 151 violations.

options.label: Full config: enable all default linters plus complexity linters
options.rationale: Maximum coverage but likely to surface many new warnings unrelated to the original violations. High risk of scope creep.

items.text: Round 1 decisions have been incorporated into plan.md: orchestrator stays in one file with phase functions, prerequisites split by platform without build tags, score target is >= 70 (not 100), GuidedFlow extracts into GuidedFlow/ directory. Plan now includes Greenfield Constraint section, Rollout/Validation Checklist, and vrooli scenario restart step in Definition of Done.

plan_updates: Incorporated all 4 round-1 settled decisions into plan. Added Greenfield Constraint section. Added Rollout/Validation Checklist with per-phase checkpoints. Added vrooli scenario restart to Definition of Done. Refined scope to explicitly note >= 70 target (not all 151 violations). Added codebase structure details from exploration.
